title: Homotopy and graded quasi-isomorphism invariance of the shift-filtered Hom complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with Hom groups in a common larger universe. All complexes below are integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] having a finite filtration interval independent of cochain degree. A filtered chain map and a filtered chain homotopy preserve every filtration step. Let $P,P'$ be bounded complexes and $I,J$ bounded-below complexes. Define the complex of abelian groups
$$C(P,I)^n=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^i,I^{i+n}),\qquad d(f)=d_If-(-1)^nf d_P,$$
with shift filtration
$$F^rC(P,I)^n=\{f\mid f^i(F^aP^i)\subseteq F^{a+r}I^{i+n}\text{ for every }a,i\}.$$
This is a bounded-below complex with a uniformly finite filtration. Precomposition by a filtered chain map $s:P'\to P$ and postcomposition by a filtered chain map $u:I\to J$ give filtered chain maps $s^*:C(P,I)\to C(P',I)$ and $u_*:C(P,I)\to C(P,J)$, commuting with one another and respecting identities and composition. Filtered-homotopic maps $s,t$ induce filtered-homotopic maps $s^*,t^*$, and filtered-homotopic maps $u,v$ induce filtered-homotopic maps $u_*,v_*$. In particular a filtered homotopy equivalence in either variable induces a filtered homotopy equivalence of these Hom complexes.

Suppose each $\operatorname{gr}^aI^n$ is injective in the extension-property sense [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If $s:P'\to P$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism, meaning that every $\operatorname{gr}^as$ is an ordinary quasi-isomorphism, then $s^*:C(P,I)\to C(P',I)$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism. These assertions concern the concrete Hom complexes and their maps before localization.

source.place: §5.1.5, pp.40–41, explicit resolution-model invariance needed for the filtered RHom lift; Stacks derived.tex Tag 05TY (lemma-morphisms-into-filtered-injective-complex) and Tag 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), applied to the graded Hom complexes. The signed homotopy calculation and shift-filtration refinement are written out in report.md.

proof.text: Use the Hom abelian groups and bilinear composition of [def-sp-abelian]. Since $P^i=0$ outside a finite interval $[p_0,p_1]$, every displayed sum over $i$ is finite and is also the product of those groups. The formula in the statement gives an additive differential: expanding $d^2f$ gives $d_I^2f=0$, $fd_P^2=0$, and two mixed terms with opposite signs. If $I^j=0$ for $j<i_0$, then $C(P,I)^n=0$ for $n<i_0-p_1$. This proves boundedness below, and applies to each of the other pairs in the statement.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text: Choose filtration bounds $F^aP=P$, $F^{b+1}P=0$, $F^cI=I$, $F^{d+1}I=0$, independent of cochain degree. The defining conditions for $F^rC$ are additive, and $d_If$ and $fd_P$ both send $F^pP$ into $F^{p+r}I$, because the two differentials preserve their filtrations [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Thus these subgroups form a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes. For $r\le c-b$ every map satisfies the condition: for $p\le b$ its target filtration step is all of $I$, and for $p>b$ its source is zero. For $r\ge d+1-a$, applying the condition to $F^aP=P$ forces every component to be zero. These are uniform filtration bounds, independent of $n$.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text: Set $(s^*f)^i=f^is^i$ and $(u_*f)^i=u^{i+n}f^i$ for $f\in C(P,I)^n$. The chain-map identities $d_Ps=sd_{P'}$ and $d_Ju=ud_I$ give $d(s^*f)=s^*(df)$ and $d(u_*f)=u_*(df)$ by substitution. Filtration preservation of $s$ and $u$ gives preservation of each shift filtration step. Associativity gives $u_*(s^*f)=s^*(u_*f)$, identity maps act as identities, $(s\circ s')^*=(s')^*s^*$, and $(u'\circ u)_*=u'_*u_*$. These arguments use only componentwise composition.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text:
Let $s-t=d_Ph+hd_{P'}$, with $h^i:P'^i\to P^{i-1}$ preserving the filtration. For homogeneous $f$ of degree $n$, define $S^n(f)=(-1)^nf h$. It has degree $n-1$ and preserves $F^rC$ for every $r$. Direct expansion gives
$$dS^n(f)=(-1)^nd_Ifh+fh d_{P'},\qquad S^{n+1}(df)=(-1)^{n+1}d_Ifh+fd_Ph.$$
Their sum is $f(s-t)=(s^*-t^*)f$. Thus $S$ is the required filtered homotopy; the degree-dependent sign is essential.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text:
If $u-v=d_Jk+kd_I$ for a filtration-preserving degree-$-1$ family $k:I\to J$, put $T^n(f)=kf$. Then
$$dT^n(f)=d_Jkf+(-1)^nkfd_P,\qquad T^{n+1}(df)=kd_If-(-1)^nkfd_P.$$
The sum is $(u-v)f$, and $T$ preserves every $F^rC$. For a filtered homotopy equivalence, apply Step 3 to its inverse and Steps 4 or 5 to its two inverse-homotopies. The induced composites are therefore filtered-homotopic to the identities, as required in either variable.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text:
For the remaining assertion assume every $\operatorname{gr}^qI^j$ is injective. Apply [lem-trf-injective-target-hom-symbol] to $X=P^i$, $Y=I^{i+n}$ and sum over the finitely many nonzero terms of $P$. Quotienting its exact symbol sequences and rearranging the finite sums gives a degreewise isomorphism
$$\sigma_r:\operatorname{gr}^r C(P,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_p C(\operatorname{gr}^pP,\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}I).$$
On the $(p,i)$ component, the symbol of $df$ is $d_{\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}I}\sigma_r(f)_{p,i}-(-1)^n\sigma_r(f)_{p,i+1}d_{\operatorname{gr}^pP}$, by the definition of the quotient differentials [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Hence this is an isomorphism of complexes. Naturality of the symbol sequence identifies the map induced by $s^*$ with the direct sum of $(\operatorname{gr}^ps)^*$. This comparison is canonical; no splitting of the differential is being chosen.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; symbol-sequence consequence isolated in lem-trf-injective-target-hom-symbol, and componentwise quotient-differential calculation

proof.text:
For bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$, the ordinary Hom complex satisfies
$$H^nC(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,B[n]),$$
naturally under precomposition. Indeed $df=0$ is precisely $d_Bf=(-1)^nfd_A$, the chain-map equation to $B[n]$ with differential $(-1)^nd_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A boundary has the form $d_Bh+(-1)^nhd_A$; the corresponding chain homotopy to $B[n]$ is $(-1)^nh$. Conversely every such homotopy gives that boundary. Addition and precomposition act on the same component families on both sides, proving the asserted naturality. All component families have finite support because $A$ is bounded.

source.place: §5.1.5, explicit finite-filtered Hom resolution model; agent calculation before localization

proof.text: Fix $p,r,n$, put $A=\operatorname{gr}^pP$, $A'=\operatorname{gr}^pP'$, and $B=\operatorname{gr}^{p+r}I$. The complexes $A,A'$ are bounded and $B[n]$ is bounded below with injective terms: taking subquotients preserves zero terms, and shifting reindexes these injective terms. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] applies to $B[n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the two homotopy-category Hom groups of Step 7 identify bijectively with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QA,Q(B[n]))$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QA',Q(B[n]))$. Their comparison is precomposition by $Q(\operatorname{gr}^ps)$, which is invertible since $\operatorname{gr}^ps$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its inverse is precomposition by $Q(\operatorname{gr}^ps)^{-1}$. Consequently every $H^n((\operatorname{gr}^ps)^*)$ is bijective. In the finite sum of Step 6, kernels and images of the differential are the sums of the coordinate kernels and images. Its cohomology maps are therefore finite sums of these bijections, hence bijections. Step 6 now proves that every $\operatorname{gr}^r(s^*)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
